name: SPX, the sums: the average price over the next 30 minutes, and the end price 30 and 60 minutes ahead beside it
how_to_use: Step 4 of the pipeline. The state is not the labels: it is the live answers from step 2, each rewritten by code as one sentence with how sure JEV was. Three questions ride on the same sentences in two requests sent at the same time. average_30, in a request of its own whose context line gives its flat zone in index points for this read, is the phone's call: where the average price over the next 30 minutes sits against the price now, every minute counting equally, graded on that average (spx_jev/integral.py) and blended half and half in code with how often the average over the same window ended up, down or flat at this time of day on the last 20 SPX sessions (spx_jev/clock.py, counted on the average price only). next_30 and next_60, the end-price sums, are asked in the other request exactly as before and are kept beside the call: next_30, blended with the end-price odds, is still the sum the question weights learn from, and next_60 is graded beside it so the two horizons can be compared. All are forecasts, graded by the bars, never acted on. Every flat zone is sized at each read from the day's own tape and the VIX, in index points (spx_jev/flat_zone.py), so that on the prior sessions the box lands flat at its base rate (spx_jev/cuts.py, spec/cuts.json); the number is filled into each question's text ({zone_points}) and named in the context, and the grader sets the box against the same number.

next_30.ask: Where is price at the end of the next 30 minutes?
next_30.why: The end-price box the question weights and the learning loop learn from, kept beside the call; the sum, not another part.
next_30.instructions: Read `context.flat_zone` for how many index points either way count as flat over each horizon this read, then `answers`, one sentence per question JEV has already answered about this moment, each ending with how sure it was. Taken together, where is price at the end of the next 30 minutes? Answer up, down, flat or unsure.

criteria.up: price ends more than {zone_points} points above where it is now; on this index that happens about {next_30_up_pct}% of the time
criteria.down: price ends more than {zone_points} points below where it is now; on this index that happens about {next_30_down_pct}% of the time
criteria.flat: price ends within {zone_points} points of where it is now, either way; on this index that is the common case, about {next_30_flat_pct}% of the time
criteria.unsure: the answers pull hard both ways, so neither the common case nor a direction can be backed

next_60.ask: Where is price at the end of the next 60 minutes?
next_60.why: The same sum at twice the horizon, graded beside the 30-minute one so the two can be compared; it never reaches the phone's headline.
next_60.instructions: Read `context.flat_zone` for how many index points either way count as flat over each horizon this read, then `answers`, one sentence per question JEV has already answered about this moment, each ending with how sure it was. Taken together, where is price at the end of the next 60 minutes? Answer up, down, flat or unsure.

criteria.up: price ends more than {zone_points} points above where it is now; on this index that happens about {next_60_up_pct}% of the time
criteria.down: price ends more than {zone_points} points below where it is now; on this index that happens about {next_60_down_pct}% of the time
criteria.flat: price ends within {zone_points} points of where it is now, either way; on this index that is the common case, about {next_60_flat_pct}% of the time
criteria.unsure: the answers pull hard both ways, so neither the common case nor a direction can be backed

average_30.ask: Where does the average price over the next {window_minutes} minutes sit against the price now?
average_30.why: What the call is graded on: the average of every minute's price over the window, so the phone's call and its grade are about the same thing. Three options, no unsure.
average_30.instructions: Read `context.average` for the price at this read, what the average over the window is and how many index points either way count as flat for this read, then `answers`, one sentence per question JEV has already answered about this moment, each ending with how sure it was. Taken together, where will the average price over the next {window_minutes} minutes sit against the price now? Answer up, down or flat.

criteria.up: the average price over the next {window_minutes} minutes sits more than {zone_points} points above the price now
criteria.down: the average price over the next {window_minutes} minutes sits more than {zone_points} points below the price now
criteria.flat: the average price over the next {window_minutes} minutes sits within {zone_points} points of the price now, either way
